facts.content: Patient reports having regular menses.
Patient has a history of irritable bowel syndrome.
Patient reports no prior urinary tract infections or renal problems.
Patient reports no prior surgery.
Patient is taking Mebavin 200 mg three times daily.
Plan is for the patient to continue Mebavin 200 mg three times daily for IBS.
Patient is allergic to clindamycin.
No significant family history is reported.
Patient lives with friends.
Patient works as a support worker.
Patient drinks approximately one glass of wine per week.
Patient has never smoked.

Assessment is uncomplicated cystitis with hematuria, characterized by 6 days of dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, afebrile status, no flank pain, and maintained urine output, noted as the first episode.
facts.source_text: 1) Uncomplicated cystitis w/ hematuria — 6 d dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain; afebrile; no flank pain; passing urine; first episode

facts.content: Irritable bowel syndrome is assessed as stable on mebeverine.
Plan for cystitis includes empiric oral antibiotics for 3 days.
A prescription for antibiotics is to be sent electronically to the requested pharmacy in Knightsbridge for pickup in about one hour.
facts.source_text: eRx to requested pharmacy (Knightsbridge); pickup ~1 hr

facts.content: Patient is advised to increase fluid intake to 2.5 to 3 liters per day.
Patient may consider drinking cranberry juice.
Patient is advised to use over-the-counter urine alkalinizing sachets from the pharmacist as directed.
facts.source_text: OTC urine alkalinizing sachets from pharmacist; use as directed

facts.content: Patient is advised to obtain a thermometer and monitor temperature.

Patient is advised to contact the provider if symptoms worsen or do not improve, or if new fever, low back or loin pain, or difficulty passing urine develops, and to arrange review if episodes become recurrent.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: contact if worsening/not improving, new fever, low back/loin pain, difficulty passing urine; if recurrent episodes, arrange review

facts.content: If episodes of cystitis become recurrent, the patient should arrange a review.
